name: pythagoras-proof
title: Pythagoras' theorem (squares)
tagline: Right triangle with a square on each side and its area shown — the a²+b²=c² visual proof; hypotenuse and areas derived, square areas occlude.
description: A right-angled triangle with a square drawn outward on each of its three sides, each square's area shown — the visual proof that the square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the two legs (a² + b² = c²). You give only the two leg lengths; the hypotenuse, all three squares (including the tilted one on the hypotenuse), the right-angle mark and every area are derived and stay correct, so dragging a corner reshapes the triangle while the areas update and the relationship holds. Per-square area occlusion ("find the missing area / side"), highlighting, an optional unit, and toggles for the area numbers, the side lengths and the a² + b² = c² sum readout.
whenToUse: Reach for this to prove or visualise Pythagoras through areas — the classic squares-on-the-sides figure — rather than just compute a side (for plain "find the hypotenuse" with a right-angle mark and side labels, use geometry/triangle instead). Give the two legs as legs: { a, b } (any positive numbers, the same units); the right angle sits between them, the hypotenuse c = √(a²+b²) and the three square areas a², b², c² are all derived. By default each square shows its area and a "9 + 16 = 25" readout appears below — the punchline. Common configurations: prove it — legs 3 and 4, show every area and the sum, so pupils see 9 + 16 = 25. Find the big square — occlude the hypotenuse square (squares: [{ on: 'c', occlude: true, highlight: true }]) so pupils add the two leg areas. Find a missing leg — occlude a leg square (on: 'a') given the other leg and the hypotenuse. Answer space — show.areas: false with show.sideLengths: true draws the three empty squares with the side lengths, for pupils to fill in each area. Add unit: "cm" to read "3 cm" and "9 cm²". draggablePoints lets pupils drag a corner to resize the triangle and watch the areas change while a² + b² always equals c². Cross-block convention: keep the same legs across the blocks of one lesson so pupils track one figure; change only what is shown, occluded or highlighted. A staged build reads well: start with the bare triangle, grow the square on each side, then reveal the sum. Address the three squares by 'a' and 'b' (the legs) and 'c' (the hypotenuse). Synonyms a teacher might use: Pythagoras, Pythagoras' theorem, square on the hypotenuse, area of the squares, a squared plus b squared, proof, right-angled triangle, hypotenuse.

legs.description: The two legs (the sides that meet at the right angle). The whole figure — hypotenuse, the three squares and their areas — is derived from these.

a.description: Length of leg a (drawn up the left side). Any positive number in your chosen unit.

b.description: Length of leg b (drawn along the bottom). Any positive number in the same unit.

unit.description: Optional unit shown on the readouts, e.g. "cm" → lengths read "3 cm" and areas "9 cm²". Omit for bare numbers (9, 16, 25).

rotation.description: Rotate the whole figure anticlockwise by this many degrees, so the right angle and hypotenuse sit at a realistic exam-figure orientation instead of always flat. The triangle and its three squares rotate together; the area numbers and the right-angle mark stay upright/readable. Use it — real questions are rarely drawn with a flat base. Default 0 (right angle bottom-left, legs horizontal and vertical) reads as the textbook proof.

squares.description: Per-square overrides for the area shown on each square. Address a square by the side it sits on: 'a' and 'b' are the legs, 'c' is the hypotenuse. Omit a square to leave its area shown normally (derived).

on.description: Which square: 'a' (square on leg a), 'b' (square on leg b), 'c' (square on the hypotenuse).

label.description: Override the area text in this square — e.g. a name, or a value with units the derived number would not carry. Omit to show the derived area.

occlude.description: Render this square's area as "?" — the "find the missing area / side" hook. The square stays drawn. Default false.

highlight.description: Shade this square amber — the result, or the square in question. Default false.

areas.description: Show the area number inside each square. Default true. Set false for an answer space (empty squares).

sideLengths.description: Label the triangle's three sides with their lengths (a, b, c). Default false.

sum.description: Show the derived "a² + b² = c²" line below the figure (e.g. "9 + 16 = 25"); it reflects occlusion, so an occluded area shows as "?". Default true.

caption.description: An optional line of text centred below the figure, e.g. "The square on the hypotenuse equals the sum of the squares on the other two sides". Omit for none.

header.description: Optional short title centred above the figure; the top padding grows to clear it.

draggablePoints.description: Web-only. Let pupils drag a free corner to resize the triangle; the legs stay perpendicular (the right angle is preserved) and the side lengths and three square areas recompute live while a² + b² stays equal to c². Default false.
